youtube.commentText: Troy Jackson is right about healthcare in Maine. My late father in law had to leave Maine because of healthcare when he wasn't well, couldn't work and had to go on Medicaid. He ended up moving in with his sister in Massachusetts because Medicaid covers more there. He was terminal, but would have preferred to stay in Maine and maybe have someone to come in to give him a little help, like a homemaker/aide type person and have his care covered like it was in Massachusetts.  He was only 60 when he died during the end of full on covid. He was given 6 months and lasted 2 years with the help of the move and his wonderful sister. Still it was too bad that he couldn't have stayed in Maine. He really loved his little house across from a pond on a dirt road in the woods. My 3 sons have wonderful memories of going there to stay, going in a canoe on the pond, visiting the farm to see the animals down the road and the country fair nearby with rides and great animals that they didn't normally get to see in our suburban Massachusetts town.
